evidence.note: The Expanded Pravda likely existed by early XIII century, contains earlier chronological layers, and survives in later copies. Princely legal administration remained limited; this supports cautious comparative use, not uniform local enactment of every rule. Troitsky MSU text used here is a second-half-XIV-century witness with edition-specific numbering.

Article 23 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes a person bearing blood or bruises from one without visible marks, requiring a witness in the latter case. Evidence about who began the encounter can change the case even when injuries are visible. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Articles 21–24 of the Expanded Pravda distinguish bodily injuries; article 24 separates a fine, payment to the injured person, and a wound-treatment payment. These are distinct textual demands, not one modern damages assessment. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 27 of the Expanded Pravda separately specifies a payment for mounting another person’s horse without asking. Such use is not identical to the horse-theft case in neighbouring articles. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 36 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes killing a thief at the theft site from a thief held until daylight, whom it directs to the princely court. Killing a person whom others have already seen bound incurs a separate textual payment. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

For a denied monetary debt, article 43 of the Expanded Pravda describes producing witnesses and their oath as a route to recovering the money. A creditor’s assertion and that supporting procedure are distinct. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 44 of the Expanded Pravda singles out one merchant entrusting money to another for trade: prior witnesses are not required, and denial is addressed through the merchant’s own oath. This is a special trading case, not removal of witnesses for every loan. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 46 of the Expanded Pravda describes money lent at rez, honey at nastav, and grain at prisop. It calls for witnesses to such terms and links recovery to what the parties agreed. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 47 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes monthly interest for a short term from a different reckoning when the money remains until the year; it also links proof of debt to witnesses and the amount. Monthly interest is not presented as one indefinitely accumulating tariff. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

For multiple debts, article 51 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes an uninformed visiting trader, local creditors, and princely money. It specifies repayment priority from selling the debtor and excludes one who has taken much interest; it is not an equal division among all creditors. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 52 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes a zakup’s flight from openly leaving to seek money or approaching the prince or judges over the master’s wrong. For the latter cases it bars reduction to full slavery and says that the zakup is to receive pravda (justice or redress). Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Articles 53–54 of the Expanded Pravda distinguish property lost while the zakup is on the master’s business, theft from a shed, and livestock lost after not being driven in and secured as ordered. Textual liability depends on circumstances, not just a shortfall. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 55 of the Expanded Pravda does not equate a zakup with a fully enslaved person: a master’s sale of the zakup into full slavery leads in the text to the sold person’s freedom and a fine on the master. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 59 of the Expanded Pravda restricts an enslaved person’s witness role but allows a boyar’s tiun in necessity and a zakup in a minor dispute. These status categories are not interchangeable. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Articles 64–66 of the Expanded Pravda distinguish altering bee-tree marks, violating boundaries, and cutting a marked or boundary oak, prescribing payments for these acts. Marks and boundary trees have legal significance in the text. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

For burning a threshing barn or household yard, article 79 of the Expanded Pravda combines making good the loss with potok and razgrablenie, placing compensation before further princely action. The text distinguishes the victim’s loss from the ensuing sanction. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 86 of the Expanded Pravda singles out the estates of boyars and the druzhina: they do not pass to the prince, and daughters receive them if there are no sons. This is a status-conditioned textual rule, not a universal exclusion of daughters from inheritance. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Article 88 of the Expanded Pravda distinguishes a widow’s portion and property granted to her by her husband from his estate; it also distinguishes children’s claim to their mother’s property. A household is not depicted as undivided property of one spouse. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

For children of one mother by two husbands, article 97 of the Expanded Pravda separates paternal estates: each group receives its own father’s estate. Sharing a mother does not merge these estates into one pool. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

Articles 102–105 of the Expanded Pravda distinguish grounds for full slavery from agreed terms: marriage to an enslaved woman, service as a tiun, or taking the key without an agreement are contrasted with stipulated terms. Receiving food or an advance is separately not equated with slavery. Source assertion concerns the documentary norm only. Temporal and regional compatibility are inferred at medium confidence; no current status, guilt, court, exact tariff, order or outcome is asserted.

claim_localizations.runtime_text: Если человек пришёл с кровью или в побоях — это одно, а если следов не видно — тогда нужен видок. Но и при видимых побоях дело может обернуться иначе, если найдётся свидетель, кто первым начал драку.

If a person comes with blood or bruises, that is one thing; if there are no visible marks, then a witness is needed. But even with visible bruises, the case can turn out differently if there is a witness to who started the fight.
За телесные раны берут не одно, а порознь: продажу — плату князю, плату самому пострадавшему и особо — лечебное на его рану. Это разные взыскания, а не одна общая плата.

For bodily wounds, several things are taken, not one: a fine to the prince, a payment to the injured person himself, and separately, money for treating his wound. These are different payments, not a single lump sum.
Кто сядет на чужого коня без спросу, с того берут особую плату — это не то же самое, что украсть коня.
Whoever mounts another person's horse without asking pays a separate fee for it — that is not the same as stealing the horse.

Вора можно убить на месте кражи. А если его продержали до света, то ведут на княжий двор — там с ним разбираются. А если уже связанного вора, которого видели связанным другие люди, всё же убьют, то за это берут особый платёж.

A thief may be killed at the site of the theft. But if he is held until daylight, he is led to the prince's court to be dealt with there. And if a thief who is already bound — whom other people have seen bound — is killed anyway, a separate payment is taken for that.
Если должник отпирается от денежного долга, то получить своё можно, выставив послухов, которые под ротой подтвердят долг. Одно дело — сказать «он мне должен», и другое — доказать это послухами.
If a debtor denies owing money, the money can be recovered by bringing forth witnesses who confirm the debt under oath. Simply saying 'he owes me' is one thing — proving it with witnesses is another.

Когда один купец передаёт деньги другому купцу для торговли, послухи наперёд не нужны — так у купцов заведено. Если тот станет отпираться, дело решает его собственная рота. Так бывает только в купеческом деле, а не при всяком займе.

When one merchant hands money to another merchant for trading, witnesses are not needed beforehand — that is the custom among merchants. If he denies it, the matter is settled by his own oath. This holds only in merchant dealings, not for every loan.
Деньги дают в рост под рез, мёд — под настав, а зерно — под присоп; на такие условия зовут послухов. Что получишь назад, зависит от того, о чём стороны договорились.
Money is lent out at rez, honey at nastav, and grain at prisop; witnesses are called for such terms. What is recovered depends on what the parties agreed.

Месячный рез берут, только пока срок короткий; если же деньги остаются до года, то счёт уже другой. Доказать долг можно, если есть послухи и известна сумма. Месячный рез не растёт бесконечно сам по себе.

Monthly interest is taken only while the term is short; if the money stays out until the year is up, the reckoning is different. The debt can be proven when there are witnesses and the amount is known. Monthly interest does not simply keep growing without end.

Если у должника много долгов, то первым получает своё приезжий торговец, который не знал о прочих его долгах, а уж после — местные заимодавцы и княжьи деньги; так делят выручку от продажи должника. Кто уже взял с должника большой рез, тому вовсе не достаётся — деньги не делят поровну между всеми.

When a debtor owes many, the visiting trader who did not know of the other debts is paid first from what the debtor is sold for; only after him come the local creditors and the prince's money. One who has already taken much interest gets nothing from this — the money is not shared out equally among everyone owed.

Если закуп тайно сбежит — это бегство. А если он открыто уйдёт искать свои деньги, либо пойдёт к князю или к судьям с жалобой на обиду от господина — это иное дело: за это его в обельные холопы не обращают, а дают ему правду.

If a zakup runs away in secret, that is flight. But if he openly leaves to seek money owed to him, or goes to the prince or the judges to complain of a wrong done by his master, that is a different matter — for this he is not turned into a full slave, but is given pravda: justice, redress.

Если закуп что-то потеряет, исполняя поручение хозяина, — это одно дело. Если товар украдут из хлева — другое. А если скотину, которую было велено загнать и запереть, закуп не загонит и она пропадёт — с него спросят иначе, чем в прочих случаях. Смотрят на обстоятельства утраты, а не только на саму пропажу.

If a zakup loses something while carrying out his master's errand, that is one matter. If goods are stolen from a shed, that is another. And if livestock that he was told to drive in and secure is lost because he did not drive it in, he answers for it differently than in the other cases. What matters is the circumstance of the loss, not only the loss itself.
Закуп — не то же самое, что обельный холоп. Если господин продаст закупа в обельное холопство, того по этому делу отпускают на волю, а с господина берут плату за то, что он сделал.
A zakup is not the same as a fully enslaved person. If a master sells a zakup into full slavery, the zakup is set free on this account, and a payment is taken from the master for what he did.
Холопа в послухи не берут. Но если нужда велика, можно взять боярского тиуна, а в малой тяжбе — закупа. Это разные случаи, один другого не заменяет.
A kholop is not taken as a witness. But in great need, a boyar's tiun may be taken, and in a minor dispute, a zakup. These are different cases, and one does not substitute for another.

За перевод бортного знака платят одно, за снос межи — другое, а за подрубку отмеченного или межевого дуба — своё; каждое разбирают порознь. Бортный знак и межевое дерево — это межа, и трогать их без права нельзя.

Altering a bee-tree mark, breaking a boundary, and cutting down a marked or boundary oak are each answered with their own payment — every one of these is judged apart. A bee-tree mark and a boundary tree mark the line, and no one may touch them without right.
Кто сожжёт гумно или двор, того отдают на поток и разграбление, но прежде отдают хозяину за его потерю — сперва возмещают убыток, а уже потом вершится дальнейшая княжеская расправа над виновным.

Whoever burns a threshing barn or a household yard is sent into exile with his goods seized, but first the owner is paid for his loss — the loss is made good before the prince deals further with the guilty man.
У бояр и у дружины наследство не отходит к князю: если сыновей нет, его получают дочери.
For boyars and for the druzhina, the estate does not go to the prince — if there are no sons, the daughters receive it.

Вдовья доля и то, что муж ей особо дал при жизни — это не то же, что его наследство. А что после матери останется — то причитается её детям особо. Хозяйство в семье — не нераздельное владение одного из супругов.

A widow's portion, and what her husband gave her separately in his lifetime, is not the same as his estate. And whatever remains after the mother belongs separately to her children. Household property is not the undivided holding of just one spouse.
У детей одной матери, но от разных отцов — каждое наследство своё: одни получают наследство своего отца, другие — своего. Общая мать не сливает эти наследства в одно.

For children of one mother but different fathers, each inheritance stays its own: one group receives the estate of their own father, the other the estate of theirs. A shared mother does not merge these estates into one.

В холопство обельное человек попадает без ряда — если женится на робе, пойдёт в тиуны или возьмёт ключ, не оговорив условий заранее. А если условия оговорены рядом наперёд, то это иное дело. Кто просто взял хлеб или дачу от хозяина, тот холопом от этого не становится.

A person falls into full slavery without an agreement — by marrying an enslaved woman, taking service as a tiun, or taking up the key without settling terms beforehand. But if the terms are settled by agreement in advance, that is a different matter. Simply taking bread or an advance from a master does not by itself make a person a slave.
